# QuantMedia

> Verified quantitative finance code. Implementations of VPIN, Hierarchical
> Risk Parity and the Probabilistic Sharpe Ratio, each run against a synthetic
> input whose correct answer is known in advance, with a dated report of what
> the code got right, what it got wrong, and what was fixed. Plus two daily
> metrics computed by the same pipeline discipline, published with their
> freshness state.

Everything on the site is free to read and free to cite with attribution.
There is no paywall, no registration, and no AI-crawler block. Author:
Cemil Ertürk (https://quantmedia.io/author/cemil-erturk.html). Independent;
not peer reviewed; no affiliation with any fund, broker or exchange.

## Verification reports (primary source)

These document defects found by executing code against known ground truth.
Every number is unedited console output from the public repository.

- [Reports index](https://quantmedia.io/reports/): what a report contains,
  and how to reproduce every published figure in one command
- [VPIN verification](https://quantmedia.io/reports/vpin-example.html): balanced
  segment 0.3292 vs informed 0.6376 (1.94x); BVC 0.4410 vs tick rule 0.1779 on
  identical data; defect: degenerate tape returned zero toxicity, fixed
- [HRP verification](https://quantmedia.io/reports/hrp-example.html):
  out-of-sample volatility drift HRP +1.3% vs minimum variance +13.6%, shrunk
  +7.7%, equal weight -2.1%; defects: pandas-3 read-only view, asymmetric
  distance matrix, both fixed
- [PSR verification](https://quantmedia.io/reports/psr-worked-example.html):
  the site's own published example was wrong (denominators 1.000 / 2.318;
  correct 1.4577 / 2.4850); corrected against scipy with every intermediate

## Implementations

- [Reproducibility index](https://quantmedia.io/reproducibility.html): which
  methods have runnable code and tests, and which papers are research-only
- Repository: https://github.com/certurk23/certurk23.github.io/tree/main/quantmedia-research
  `python quantmedia-research/verify_examples.py` re-runs both packages and
  asserts every shipped output matches to nine decimal places. 28 tests.
- [PSR calculator](https://quantmedia.io/tools/probabilistic-sharpe-ratio-calculator.html):
  computes rather than quotes; shows every intermediate value

## Original daily data

Computed by QuantMedia after each US close from a 30-signal scan of 180
liquid US-listed equities; regenerated daily; never backfilled. Each has a
machine-readable JSON companion. The scan itself is a demonstration of the
pipeline discipline, has no forward-tested track record, and is not a signal
service.

- [Signal Breadth Index](https://quantmedia.io/indices/signal-breadth.html):
  share of scored equities meeting a 22-of-30 threshold.
  JSON: /data/signal_breadth.json, history: /data/breadth_history.json
- [Sector Confluence](https://quantmedia.io/indices/sector-confluence.html):
  mean score and BUY breadth per sector. JSON: /data/sector_confluence.json
- Engine parameters, canonical: /data/signal_config.json
- Pipeline freshness state: /data/status.json

## Research papers

Five papers with stated assumptions, measured results where code exists,
robustness discussion, limitations and primary references:
VPIN, Hierarchical Risk Parity, Probabilistic Sharpe Ratio, slippage and
latency modelling, bid-ask spread dynamics. Index: https://quantmedia.io/papers.html

## What is deliberately not here

No live VPIN readings for any real security: that needs tick data this site
does not have. No latency measurements from co-located hardware: there is
none. No performance claims for the daily scan: no track record exists and
none is claimed. See https://quantmedia.io/editorial-policy.html for data
sources, funding, the corrections policy and the use of AI tools.
